items.title: 3.5 Atomic orbital hybridization and shapes of molecules

source_refs.note: Topic 3.5, printed page 61, with the Keep in Mind box.

blocks.title: Hybridization
blocks.text: A process in which atomic orbitals of slightly different energies and shapes are mixed together to form a new set of equivalent orbitals of the same energy and the same shape.

items: Hybridization is a process of mixing orbitals in a single atom (or ion).
Only orbitals of comparable (relatively close) energies can be mixed to form hybrid orbitals.
The number of mixing orbitals is always equal to the number of resulting hybrid orbitals.

blocks.prompt: Carbon's 2s orbital and its 2p orbitals can hybridize, but its 1s orbital does not join them. Why?
blocks.explanation: Only orbitals of comparable energy mix. The 2s and 2p orbitals are close in energy, so they can blend into equivalent hybrids; the 1s orbital lies far below them in energy and stays as it is.

items: Hybridization mixes orbitals of one atom that are close in energy into the same number of equivalent hybrid orbitals of equal energy and shape.
